verses.zh: 以下也是所罗门的箴言，是犹大王希西家的人所誊录的。
verses.kjv: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.en: These are more of Solomon's wise sayings, copied out by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

verses.zh: 将事隐秘乃神的荣耀；将事察清乃君王的荣耀。
verses.kjv: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.en: It is God's glory to keep a matter hidden, and a king's glory to search a matter out.

verses.zh: 天之高，地之厚，君王之心也测不透。
verses.kjv: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.en: The sky is high, the earth is deep, and a king's heart cannot be worked out either.

verses.zh: 除去银子的渣滓就有银子出来，银匠能以做器皿。
verses.kjv: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
verses.en: Take the waste out of the silver, and the silversmith can make a beautiful dish.

verses.zh: 除去王面前的恶人，国位就靠公义坚立。
verses.kjv: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.en: Take bad people away from the king, and his throne will stand firm on doing right.

verses.zh: 不要在王面前妄自尊大；不要在大人的位上站立。
verses.kjv: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
verses.en: Do not push yourself forward in front of the king, or stand in the place meant for important people.

verses.zh: 宁可有人说：请你上来，强如在你觐见的王子面前叫你退下。
verses.kjv: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.en: It is better to be told "Come up here" than to be moved down in front of a prince you can see.

verses.zh: 不要冒失出去与人争竞，免得至终被他羞辱，你就不知道怎样行了。
verses.kjv: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
verses.en: Do not rush off to start an argument, or you may not know what to do when your neighbour shames you in the end.

verses.zh: 你与邻舍争讼，要与他一人辩论，不可泄漏人的密事，
verses.kjv: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
verses.en: If you have a disagreement, settle it with that person alone, and do not give away someone else's secret,

verses.zh: 恐怕听见的人骂你，你的臭名就难以脱离。
verses.kjv: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
verses.en: or whoever hears it will shame you, and your bad name will stick.

verses.zh: 一句话说得合宜，就如金苹果在银网子里。
verses.kjv: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
verses.en: A word spoken at just the right time is like golden apples in a silver setting.

verses.zh: 智慧人的劝戒，在顺从的人耳中，好像金耳环和精金的妆饰。
verses.kjv: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.en: A wise correction to a listening ear is like a gold earring or fine gold jewellery.

verses.zh: 忠信的使者叫差他的人心里舒畅，就如在收割时有冰雪的凉气。
verses.kjv: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.en: A trustworthy messenger refreshes whoever sent him, like the coolness of snow at harvest time.

verses.zh: 空夸赠送礼物的，好像无雨的风云。
verses.kjv: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
verses.en: Someone who boasts about gifts they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.

verses.zh: 恒常忍耐可以劝动君王；柔和的舌头能折断骨头。
verses.kjv: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.en: Patience can win over a ruler, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.

verses.zh: 你得了蜜吗？只可吃够而已，恐怕你过饱就呕吐出来。
verses.kjv: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.en: Have you found honey? Eat just enough — too much and you will be sick.

verses.zh: 你的脚要少进邻舍的家，恐怕他厌烦你，恨恶你。
verses.kjv: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour’s house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
verses.en: Do not go to your neighbour's house too often, or he will get tired of you and start to dislike you.

verses.zh: 作假见证陷害邻舍的，就是大槌，是利刀，是快箭。
verses.kjv: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.en: Telling lies about your neighbour is like a heavy hammer, a sword, and a sharp arrow.

verses.zh: 患难时倚靠不忠诚的人，好像破坏的牙，错骨缝的脚。
verses.kjv: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.en: Trusting an unreliable person in trouble is like a broken tooth or a foot that gives way.

verses.zh: 对伤心的人唱歌，就如冷天脱衣服，又如硷上倒醋。
verses.kjv: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
verses.en: Singing cheerful songs to a sad heart is like taking someone's coat away in cold weather, or pouring vinegar on soda.

verses.zh: 你的仇敌若饿了，就给他饭吃；若渴了，就给他水喝；
verses.kjv: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.en: If your enemy is hungry, give him food; if he is thirsty, give him water,

verses.zh: 因为，你这样行就是把炭火堆在他的头上；耶和华也必赏赐你。
verses.kjv: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
verses.en: because doing that heaps burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.

verses.zh: 北风生雨，谗谤人的舌头也生怒容。
verses.kjv: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
verses.en: The north wind brings rain, and a gossiping tongue brings angry faces.

verses.zh: 宁可住在房顶的角上，不在宽阔的房屋与争吵的妇人同住。
verses.kjv: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
verses.en: Better to live in a corner of the roof than share a big house with someone always quarrelling.

verses.zh: 有好消息从远方来，就如拿凉水给口渴的人喝。
verses.kjv: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
verses.en: Good news from a faraway country is like cold water to someone very thirsty.

verses.zh: 义人在恶人面前退缩，好像趟浑之泉，弄浊之井。
verses.kjv: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
verses.en: A good person who gives way to a bad one is like a muddied spring or a spoiled well.

verses.zh: 吃蜜过多是不好的；考究自己的荣耀也是可厌的。
verses.kjv: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
verses.en: Eating too much honey is not good, and neither is chasing after your own glory.

verses.zh: 人不制伏自己的心，好像毁坏的城邑没有墙垣。
verses.kjv: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
verses.en: Someone who cannot control their own temper is like a city with its walls broken down.
